checks.s: The memo rates SOW §7.2's outright assignment of custom-deliverable IP to Helios as a High Risk deviation.
The memo recommends that Verdantis retain all background IP.
The memo recommends granting Helios a perpetual, non-exclusive license to custom deliverables, consistent with the playbook standard.
The memo notes that IP ownership is a 'must-win' issue per Priya Nandakumar / client instructions.
The memo flags the liability cap in SOW §9 as a High Risk deviation.
The memo states that the SOW liability cap is $1,132,500 (6 × $188,750).
The memo states that the playbook cap is the greater of 12 months' fees ($2,265,000) or $3,000,000, yielding $3,000,000.
The memo quantifies the liability-cap gap as $1,867,500 ($3,000,000 − $1,132,500).
The memo recommends raising the liability cap to at least $3,000,000 (the greater of 12 months' fees or $3M).
The memo flags SOW §9's one-way consequential-damages exclusion, which applies only to Helios and leaves Verdantis exposed, as a High Risk deviation.
The memo recommends a mutual exclusion of consequential, incidental, and punitive damages applicable to both parties.
The memo flags SOW §5's uncapped SLA penalties, starting at 15% of monthly fees per incident, as a High Risk deviation.
The memo recommends capping aggregate SLA credits at 10% of monthly fees per month, consistent with the playbook.
The memo flags SOW §11's one-way termination for convenience (Helios only, 30 days' notice, no wind-down fees, and no Verdantis T-for-C right) as a High Risk deviation.
The memo recommends mutual termination-for-convenience rights.
The memo recommends 90 days' written notice for termination for convenience.
The memo recommends wind-down fees for termination for convenience.
The memo flags SOW §14's undefined 'minor scope adjustments' change-order carve-out as a High Risk deviation.
The memo recommends that all scope changes require a mutual written change order with pricing adjustment.
The memo recommends defining 'minor scope adjustments' with a dollar and/or hours threshold.
The memo flags SOW §8's one-way indemnification, under which Verdantis indemnifies Helios with no reciprocal obligation, as a High Risk deviation.
The memo recommends making indemnification mutual.
The memo recommends that each party indemnify for its own negligence and IP infringement.
The memo flags SOW §10's 12-month warranty period as a Medium Risk deviation.
The memo recommends reducing the warranty to 90 days post-acceptance per deliverable, consistent with the playbook.
The memo flags SOW §13's insurance requirements as a Medium Risk deviation.
The memo states the CGL gap as $2M current vs. $5M demanded.
The memo states the umbrella gap as $5M current vs. $10M demanded.
The memo states the E&O gap as $3M current vs. $10M demanded.
The memo recommends aligning insurance requirements with playbook minimums ($2M CGL / $5M umbrella / $3M E&O) or at most Verdantis's current policy limits.
The memo flags SOW §6's acceptance-testing provision as a Medium Risk deviation.
The memo notes that SOW §6 provides 45 calendar days rather than 15 business days for acceptance testing.
The memo notes that rejection under SOW §6 is in 'sole discretion.'
The memo notes that SOW §6 allows unlimited re-performance cycles.
The memo recommends 15 business days per milestone for acceptance testing.
The memo recommends deemed acceptance absent written objection.
The memo recommends objective acceptance criteria.
The memo flags SOW §4's Net 60 payment terms as a Medium Risk deviation.
The memo recommends Net 30 as the primary payment position.
The memo recommends Net 45 as an acceptable payment compromise/fallback.
The memo flags SOW §12's data-security provision as a deviation and notes that the DPA is missing.
The memo notes that SOW §12 specifies no encryption standard.
The memo notes that SOW §12 uses vague 'industry-standard security' language.
The memo recommends replacing vague security language with a specific SOC 2 Type II requirement.
The memo recommends replacing vague security language with an AES-256 encryption-at-rest requirement.
The memo recommends attaching the Verdantis standard DPA template as an exhibit to the SOW.
The memo flags SOW §16's Virginia law / Fairfax County Circuit Court provision as a Low Risk deviation from the playbook (Delaware law / Court of Chancery).
The memo recommends Delaware law as the primary governing-law position.
The memo recommends Virginia law with federal court venue as an acceptable fallback.
The memo flags SOW §15's audit-rights provision as a Low Risk deviation and notes unlimited audits, 10 days' notice, and undefined 'material deficiency' cost-shifting.
The memo recommends limiting audits to once per 12-month period.
The memo recommends 30 days' notice for audits.
The memo recommends that audits be at the auditing party's expense.
The memo recommends guardrails to protect proprietary cost data.
The memo flags the absence of a non-solicitation provision as a Low Risk deviation.
The memo recommends adding a mutual 12-month non-solicit of personnel engaged in the SOW.
The memo notes the prior history of Helios recruiting Verdantis engineers mid-project.

The memo identifies the 14 playbook-enumerated risk-tiered deviations as 7 High Risk items, 4 Medium Risk items, and 3 Low Risk items; it does not count the separately flagged §12 data-security / missing-DPA item as a 15th item or assign it a High/Medium rating.

The redline shows tracked-changes revisions to all 14 risk-tiered deviating provisions of the Helios SOW, implementing Verdantis's preferred positions or, where the client has indicated flexibility, acceptable fallback positions; the §12 data-security / DPA markup is not counted among these 14 provisions.
The memo states that any High Risk playbook deviation requires General Counsel Sandra Yoo's personal sign-off before it can be accepted, per the playbook escalation procedure.
The memo discusses the MSA (VS-HFS-2024-0011) order-of-precedence clause, under which the MSA controls unless the SOW expressly states otherwise.
The memo identifies specific SOW provisions that may conflict with or attempt to override MSA-level protections without express language.
The memo states the Total Contract Value (TCV) as $6,480,000.
The memo states the Annual Contract Value (ACV) as $3,240,000/year.
The memo states the Phase 1 fixed fee as $1,950,000.
The memo states the Phase 1 milestone amounts as $585,000, $780,000, and $585,000.
The memo states the Phase 2 monthly fee as $188,750/month for 24 months, totaling $4,530,000.
The memo notes that Helios has potential for approximately $8M in additional SOWs in FY2026.
The memo identifies IP, liability cap, and consequential damages as must-win issues and distinguishes them from concession candidates such as payment terms/Net 45 and governing law/Virginia.
The redline proposes adding the Verdantis standard DPA template as a new exhibit to the SOW.
The redline replaces or supplements the vague 'industry-standard security' language in §12 with a specific reference to SOC 2 Type II compliance.
The redline replaces or supplements the vague 'industry-standard security' language in §12 with a specific reference to AES-256 encryption at rest.
At least one deliverable references or is dated/addressed for delivery by June 6, 2025.
At least one deliverable references the June 16, 2025 negotiation session with Helios.
